summary.headline: Bajaj Finance Q2 FY27: AUM up 26.5% to INR 5,84,624 crore, PAT up 29% to INR 6,367 crore after a INR 337 crore macro overlay.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as an excellent quarter, with AUM growth of 26.5% and net AUM addition of about INR 38,000 crore in the quarter. PBT before the new macro overlay grew 34% to INR 8,874 crore, and PAT before the overlay grew 34% to INR 6,619 crore. Asset quality was stable on management's account, with GNPA at 1.06% and NNPA at 42 bps, though Stage 2 and 3 rose INR 1,601 crore, mainly from short-tenor gold loans that management says are transient. Management guided FY27 growth to 26-27% and flagged marginal NIM moderation as two more repo hikes are assumed.

segments.name: Rural consumer finance
segments.commentary: AUM grew 63% YoY; management is pruning drought-affected districts, with Maharashtra most affected.

segments.name: MFI
segments.commentary: AUM grew 54% on a low base; MFI branches being added, with some district reductions.

segments.name: CV and tractor
segments.commentary: AUM grew 89% on a low base.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: AUM grew only 3%; management expects double-digit growth in H2 and says rising GNPA reflects a flat denominator.

segments.name: Captive book
segments.commentary: Winding down; now about INR 2,400 crore, expected to ease credit costs.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Book just above INR 24,000 crore (4.1% of balance sheet); network 2,022 branches, target about 2,800 standalone gold branches by year-end. Stage 2 rose about INR 1,047-1,100 crore from short-tenor schemes; INR 550 crore has already moved back to Stage 1.

segments.name: BHFL (Bajaj Housing Finance)
segments.commentary: Disbursements and AUM grew 25%; PAT grew 18%; opex to NTI improved to 19.1% from 19.7%; ROE 12.7% from 12.2%.

segments.name: BFSL (Bajaj Finserv Securities)
segments.commentary: PAT grew 36% and it added 121,000 customers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth expected at 26-27%; medium-term AUM growth guidance of 20-25% (long-term 23-25% reiterated).
FY27 new loans guided at 60-62 million; new customer additions of 18-20 million.
Opex-to-NTI expected to improve 25-40 bps in FY27.
NIM: management assumes two more repo hikes, implying marginal moderation; H1 NIM about 5 bps lower than March; cost of funds compression guidance of 10-15 bps now carries a marginal headwind.
Credit cost for rest of FY27 expected in the same corridor as H1; FY27 likely to be one of the lowest credit-cost years in four years.
Non-interest income: H1 grew about 20% vs 16-18% guidance; long-term fee income growth 15-18%.

Capital raise: Board approved INR 11,700 crore QIP and a Bajaj Finserv preferential issue of INR 5,800 crore (subject to shareholder approval); leverage corridor to be lowered to 5-5.5% from 5.5-6% (currently 5.1%).
capex_capacity: Gold loan network 2,022 branches after adding about 320 in Q2; target close to 2,800 standalone gold branches by FY27 end.

AI unit of 328 people; facial recognition deployed in about 534 stores and 1,163 service branches; 180-odd agentic applications and 600-odd agents targeted for the year (65 applications and about 130 agents currently).
Capital raise of INR 11,700 crore QIP plus INR 5,800 crore Bajaj Finserv preferential issue; may partly come from BHFL dilution, with a three-year timeline.
Management says it will not raise capital for dilution-driven purposes; described the raise as growth-linked, with balance sheet expected to double in three years.
BHFL monthly affordable loan disbursements (Sambhav) above INR 500 crore; expected to exit FY27 at INR 800 crore/month and reach INR 1,300-1,400 crore/month by Q3 next year.
demand_pricing: New loans grew 11% YoY to 13.5 million in Q2; 4.42 million new customers added. Franchise 129 million customers; cross-sell franchise 82 million.

Gold loans: average ticket INR 2.4-2.5 lakh, LTV held at 75% inclusive of interest; management says gold prices fell from 5,400 to 4,200 over the period. Bullet repayment is about 99% of gold loans; the company has stopped short-tenor schemes since August and will offer 9-12 month tenors plus monthly/quarterly interest options.
Competition: management says there is significant pricing noise in gold loans and intense competition in BHFL; it will not chase AUM at the cost of margin.
Management pruned B2B and MFI business in drought-hit districts, reducing CPL origination from 7% to about half in some businesses and zero where margin is lacking; monsoon at 87% of LPA.
Insurance and MDR: insurance distribution rules are at discussion-paper stage; management is building multiple scenarios and says open architecture decision awaits final regulations.

qa_highlights.question: Why not offer short-term gold loans, and will two-wheeler customers be part of the cross-sell franchise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said short tenors push customers into delinquency and auction; it is moving to 9-12 month bullet tenors plus monthly/quarterly interest options. On two-wheeler customers, management said yes, pool quality is likely to be lower, but it wants open-architecture two-wheeler finance at 30-35% of credit cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the MSME GNPA increase and the 10 bps GNPA rise in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: MSME GNPA rose on a flat denominator (3% growth), with 3/6/9 MOB trends near 2019 levels after origination changes from July 2025. The Q2 rise is due to 92 days in Q2 vs 91 in Q1; Stage 2+3 ex-gold improved to 1.88% from 1.9%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale for the macro overlay and what is the total overlay stock?
qa_highlights.answer: Overlay is above the ECL model and framed as resilience against cyclical credit cost swings (1.75% to 2.15% peak). The macro overlay stands at about INR 226 crore; management overlay INR 512 crore (INR 185 crore last quarter, INR 327 crore this quarter); LGD floor adds an estimated INR 350-500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 growth and margin expectations once cost of funds rises?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth 26-27%; medium-term 20-25%. NIM to moderate marginally as two more hikes are assumed; Q2 NIM was 10-12 bps below Q1; cost of funds guidance compression of 10-15 bps now carries a marginal headwind.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise such a large capital amount now, and why not dilute BHFL?
qa_highlights.answer: Capital is for growth; the balance sheet doubled in three years after a INR 10,000 crore raise, and the raise is about 17.5% of balance sheet, with core ROE of 19-20%. Part may come from BHFL dilution; BFL intends to stay at 75% vs 87% today. Leverage corridor is being lowered to 5-5.5% from 5.5-6% (currently 5.1%).

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on the RBI revolving credit draft and the insurance rules?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is awaiting final RBI rules and hopes for a middle path. If a full ban came, AUM impact would be transient and NIM and profitability marginally compressed. Term loan variants without withdrawal features will launch on 1 November.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company protecting ROA if revenue headwinds emerge in FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated long-term guidance of 20-25% profit growth and 19-21% ROE, and said levers include faster top-line growth, slower fee or opex growth and lower loan losses.

risks_watch: Gold loan Stage 2 movement (INR 1,047-1,100 crore) and tenor-shift execution; gold prices down from 5,400 to 4,200 per gram per management.
Drought and monsoon stress in rural books, with Maharashtra most affected; June-to-June LNO outlook weaker per management.
RBI revolving credit draft and insurance commission regulation could affect AUM, fees and NIM.
Cost of funds rising with two more repo hikes assumed; NIM moderation risk.
Macro overlay plus management overlay (INR 738 crore total, incl. INR 226 crore macro) and LGD floor adding INR 350-500 crore; credit cost trajectory H2.
Execution of INR 17,500 crore capital raise (INR 11,700 crore QIP plus INR 5,800 crore Bajaj Finserv preferential) and possible BHFL dilution.
key_quotes: Overall, I would say it is an excellent quarter with strong performance across all key metrics, of AUM, new customer addition, credit cost, profit growth, ROA and ROE.
We are clear we don't want to push the customer into default /delinquency and the regulations and the guidelines are very clear.
So, I think there's no dull moment since COVID, we are now used to be – or all management should be used to no dull moment in building business or running businesses.
Disbursal is a vanity number. AUM is the rightful number.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on growth, capital adequacy and credit quality, calling Q2 an excellent quarter and describing the macro overlay as resilience rather than a sign of stress. It was cautious and somewhat defensive on gold loan Stage 2 movement, MSME GNPA, NIM direction, and the RBI revolving credit draft, where it gave no firm numbers and said it was premature to speculate.
